slides.title: Patterns in binomial expansions

prompt.tex: Describe the coefficients and the powers of \(a\) and \(b\).

working.tex: The power of \(a\) decreases from \(n\) to \(0\).
The power of \(b\) increases from \(0\) to \(n\).
The powers of \(a\) and \(b\) add up to \(n\) in every term.

slides.title: Pascal’s triangle

blocks.tex: Each entry, except the outside 1s, is the sum of the two entries immediately above it.\par Memorise these first rows.
The second number tells you the power of the expansion. For \((2+x)^4\), use the row \(1,4,6,4,1\).
We will see why each row gives the coefficients of \((a+b)^n\).

slides.title: Expanding (2 + 3x)⁴

blocks.tex: Find the expansion of \((2+3x)^4\).
1. Use row 4 of Pascal’s triangle.
\[1,\quad4,\quad6,\quad4,\quad1\]
2. Use descending powers of \(2\), from 4 to 0.
\[2^4,\quad2^3,\quad2^2,\quad2,\quad1\]
3. Multiply by ascending powers of \(3x\), from 0 to 4.
\[1,\quad3x,\quad(3x)^2,\quad(3x)^3,\quad(3x)^4\]
Write one term per line while working. Raise every factor in a bracket to the indicated power before simplifying.

slides.title: Finding a single coefficient

blocks.tex: The coefficient of \(x^2\) in \((2-cx)^5\) is 720. Find the possible values of \(c\).
Row 5 is \(1,5,10,10,5,1\). Counting the first entry as entry 0, the coefficient at entry 2 is \(10\).
Use \((-cx)^2\) to obtain \(x^2\). The other power is \(2^3\), because the powers add up to 5.
\[\begin{aligned}80c^2&=720\\c^2&=9\\c&=\pm3\end{aligned}\]

slides.title: Test your understanding

blocks.tex: (a) Find the first three terms, in ascending powers of \(x\), of \((2+kx)^7\), where \(k\) is a constant. Give each term in its simplest form. (4 marks)\par Given that the coefficient of \(x^2\) is six times the coefficient of \(x\), (b) find \(k\). (2 marks)
\[\begin{aligned}(2+kx)^7&=2^7+\binom71 2^6(kx)+\binom72 2^5(kx)^2+\cdots\\&=128+448kx+672k^2x^2+\cdots\end{aligned}\]
\[\begin{aligned}672k^2&=6(448k)\\672k(k-4)&=0\\k&=4\end{aligned}\]
The zero value does not give three non-zero terms.

slides.title: Exercise 8A · Questions 6 and 7

prompt.tex: 6 The coefficient of \(x^2\) in the expansion of \((2+ax)^3\) is 54. Find the possible values of the constant \(a\).

working.tex: \((2+ax)^3\) has coefficients \(1\ 3\ \mathbf3\ 1\).\par The bold number is the coefficient of the term \(2(ax)^2\).\par Term in \(x^2\) is \(3\times2(ax)^2=6a^2x^2\).\par Coefficient of \(x^2\) is \(6a^2\).\par So \(6a^2=54,\ a^2=9,\ a=\pm3\).

prompt.tex: 7 The coefficient of \(x^3\) in the expansion of \((2-x)(3+bx)^3\) is 45. Find possible values of the constant \(b\).

working.tex: Source discrepancy: the supplied working uses the coefficient of x². The question shown asks for x³. The working below follows the question as written.

blocks.tex: \((3+bx)^3\) has coefficients and terms\[\begin{array}{rrrr}1&3&3&1\\3^3&3^2(bx)&3(bx)^2&(bx)^3\end{array}\]\[\begin{aligned}(3+bx)^3&=1\times3^3+3\times3^2bx+3\times3(bx)^2+1\times(bx)^3\\&=27+27bx+9b^2x^2+b^3x^3\end{aligned}\]So \((2-x)(3+bx)^3=(2-x)(27+27bx+9b^2x^2+b^3x^3)\).

Term in \(x^2\) is \(2\times9b^2x^2-x\times27bx=18b^2x^2-27bx^2\).\par Coefficient of \(x^2\) is \(18b^2-27b\).\par So\[\begin{aligned}18b^2-27b&=45\\2b^2-3b&=5\\2b^2-3b-5&=0\\(2b-5)(b+1)&=0\\b&=\tfrac52,-1\end{aligned}\]

blocks.tex: 8 Work out the coefficient of \(x^2\) in the expansion of \((p-2x)^3\). Give your answer in terms of \(p\).
\(500\left(1+\dfrac X{100}\right)^5\)
9 After 5 years, the value of an investment of \(\pounds500\) at an interest rate of \(X\%\) per annum is given by
Find an approximation for this expression in the form \(A+BX+CX^2\), where \(A,B\) and \(C\) are constants to be found. You can ignore higher powers of \(X\).
The coefficients are \(1,3,\mathbf3,1\).\par The term in \(x^2\) is \(3(p)(-2x)^2=12px^2\).\par So the coefficient of the term \(x^2\) is \(12p\).

\[500\left(1+\frac X{100}\right)^5\]The coefficients are \(1,5,10,10,5,1\).\[\begin{aligned}500\left(1+\frac X{100}\right)^5&=500\left(1(1)^5+5(1)^4\left(\frac X{100}\right)+10(1)^3\left(\frac X{100}\right)^2+\ldots\right)\\&=500\left(1+\frac X{20}+\frac{X^2}{1000}+\ldots\right)\\&\approx500+25X+\frac{X^2}2\end{aligned}\]\[A=500,B=25,C=\tfrac12\]

slides.title: Extension · A binomial equation

blocks.tex: How many pairs of positive integers \(x,y\) satisfy\[x^3+6x^2y+12xy^2+8y^3=2^{30}?\]
A) \(0\)\par B) \(2^6\)\par C) \(2^9-1\)\par D) \(2^{10}+2\)\par E) — (blank in the supplied slide)
For \(x\) and \(y\) to be positive integers, \(y\) can be any integer from 1 to \(2^9-1\). There are \(2^9-1\) pairs. The answer is C.

slides.title: Factorial and the choose function

blocks.tex: \[n!=n(n-1)\cdots2\cdot1\]Say “n factorial”. It counts the ways of arranging \(n\) distinct objects in a line.
Three letters A, B and C have \(3\times2\times1=3!=6\) arrangements. Use the factorial button on your calculator.
\[\binom nr=\frac{n!}{r!(n-r)!}\]Say “n choose r”. It counts selections of \(r\) objects from \(n\), when order does not matter.
Choosing four people from ten gives \(\binom{10}4=\frac{10!}{4!6!}=210\) selections. Use the nCr button. The \(\binom nr\) notation is preferable in written work.

slides.title: Binomial coefficients and Pascal’s triangle

blocks.tex: Number the top row 0 and the first entry 0. Entry \(k\) in row \(n\) is \(\binom nk\). The top number gives the row. The bottom number gives the entry.
For large powers, such as \((x+3)^{20}\), calculate coefficients with the choose function rather than building all the rows.
\[\binom41=\binom43\]
The triangle is symmetric. Choosing one object is equivalent to choosing the three objects to leave out.
The textbook calls the top row the first row. In these lessons we use row 0, so row and entry numbers match the binomial coefficient directly.

slides.title: Pascal’s rule

blocks.tex: This is useful enrichment for STEP. You are not required to know the proof for this course.
\[\binom31+\binom32=\binom42\]
\[\binom{n-1}{k-1}+\binom{n-1}k=\binom nk\]
To choose \(k\) items from \(n\), consider the first item. If it is chosen, select the remaining \(k-1\) from \(n-1\). If it is not chosen, select all \(k\) from \(n-1\). Add the two disjoint cases.

\textbf{Challenge}\par a Work out \({}^{10}C_3\) and \({}^{10}C_7\).\par b Work out \({}^{14}C_5\) and \({}^{14}C_9\).\par c What do you notice about your answers to parts \textbf{a} and \textbf{b}?\par d Prove that \({}^{n}C_r={}^{n}C_{n-r}\).

\textbf{a}\[{}^{10}C_3=\frac{10!}{3!7!}=120,\quad{}^{10}C_7=\frac{10!}{7!3!}=120\]\textbf{b}\[{}^{14}C_5=\frac{14!}{5!9!}=2002,\quad{}^{14}C_9=\frac{14!}{9!5!}=2002\]\textbf{c} The two answers for part \textbf{a} are the same and the two answers for part \textbf{b} are the same.\par\textbf{d} \({}^{n}C_r=\frac{n!}{r!(n-r)!}\) and \({}^{n}C_{n-r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!r!}\) because \(\frac{n!}{(n-r)!(n-(n-r))!}\) and \((n-(n-r))=r\).\par As \(\frac{n!}{r!(n-r)!}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!r!},\ {}^nC_r={}^nC_{n-r}\).

slides.title: Why binomial coefficients count the terms

blocks.tex: The entries in row 5 are \(1,5,10,10,5,1\), or \(\binom50,\binom51,\ldots,\binom55\).
Every term comes from choosing one term from each bracket. How many choices produce \(a^3b^2\)?
Choose three of the five brackets to contribute \(a\). The other two contribute \(b\).
\[\text{The resulting term is }10a^3b^2.\]
This is why Pascal’s triangle gives the coefficients in a binomial expansion.

slides.title: The binomial expansion formula

blocks.tex: \[(a+b)^n=\sum_{r=0}^{n}\binom nr a^{n-r}b^r\]
For \(n\) a non-negative integer, each term is \(\binom nr a^{n-r}b^r\). The two powers add up to \(n\). Fractional and negative powers are studied in Year 2.

slides.title: Exercise 8D · Question 5

blocks.tex: When \((1-2x)^p\) is expanded, the coefficient of \(x^2\) is 40. Given that \(p>0\), find (a) \(p\), (b) the coefficient of \(x\), and (c) the coefficient of \(x^3\).

\textbf{a}\[(1-2x)^p=1^p+\binom p1 1^{p-1}(-2x)+\binom p2 1^{p-2}(-2x)^2+\ldots\]\[\binom p1=\frac{p!}{1!(p-1)!}=p,\qquad\binom p2=\frac{p!}{2!(p-2)!}=\frac{p(p-1)}2\]\[\begin{aligned}\text{So }(1-2x)^p&=1+p(-2x)+\frac{p(p-1)}2(-2x)^2+\ldots\\&=1-2px+2p(p-1)x^2+\ldots\end{aligned}\]\[\begin{aligned}x^2\text{ term}&=2p(p-1)x^2\\2p(p-1)&=40\\p^2-p-20&=0\\(p-5)(p+4)&=0\end{aligned}\]\(p>0\), so \(p=5\).

\textbf{b} Coefficient of \(x=-2p=-10\).\par\textbf{c}\[\begin{aligned}x^3\text{ term}&=\binom p3 1^{p-3}(-2x)^3\\&=\frac{p(p-1)(p-2)}{3!}(-2x)^3\\&=\frac{5\times4\times3}{3!}(-8x^3)\\&=-80x^3\end{aligned}\]Coefficient of \(x^3=-80\).

blocks.tex: 6 a Find the first three terms, in ascending powers of \(x\), of the binomial expansion of \((5+px)^{30}\), where \(p\) is a non-zero constant.\par b Given that in this expansion the coefficient of \(x^2\) is 29 times the coefficient of \(x\) work out the value of \(p\).

7 a Find the first four terms, in ascending powers of \(x\), of the binomial expansion of \((1+qx)^{10}\), where \(q\) is a non-zero constant.\par b Given that in the expansion of \((1+qx)^{10}\) the coefficient of \(x^3\) is 108 times the coefficient of \(x\), work out the value of \(q\).

\textbf{a}\[\begin{aligned}(1+qx)^{10}&=1^{10}+\binom{10}1 1^9(qx)+\binom{10}2 1^8(qx)^2+\binom{10}3 1^7(qx)^3+\ldots\\&=1+10qx+45q^2x^2+120q^3x^3+\ldots\end{aligned}\]\textbf{b} Coefficient of \(x^3\) is \(120q^3\). Coefficient of \(x\) is \(10q\).\[\begin{aligned}\text{So }120q^3&=108\times10q\\\Rightarrow120q^3-1080q&=0\\\Rightarrow120q(q^2-9)&=0\\\Rightarrow120q(q+3)(q-3)&=0\\q=0,\ q=-3&\text{ or }q=3\end{aligned}\]But as \(q\) is non-zero, \(q=\pm3\).

8 a Find the first three terms, in ascending powers of \(x\), of the binomial expansion of \((1+px)^{11}\), where \(p\) is a constant.\par b The first 3 terms in the same expansion are \(1,77x\) and \(qx^2\), where \(q\) is a constant. Find the value of \(p\) and the value of \(q\).

9 a Write down the first three terms, in ascending powers of \(x\), of the binomial expansion of \((1+px)^{15}\), where \(p\) is a non-zero constant.\par b Given that, in the expansion of \((1+px)^{15}\), the coefficient of \(x\) is \((-q)\) and the coefficient of \(x^2\) is \(5q\), find the value of \(p\) and the value of \(q\).

\textbf{a}\[\begin{aligned}(1+px)^{15}&=1^{15}+\binom{15}1 1^{14}(px)^1+\binom{15}2 1^{13}(px)^2+\ldots\\&=1+15px+105p^2x^2+\ldots\end{aligned}\]\textbf{b} \(15p=-q\) and \(105p^2=5q\).\[21p^2=q\]Substituting \(15p=-q\) into \(21p^2=q\):\[\begin{aligned}21p^2&=-15p\\21p^2+15p&=0\\3p(7p+5)&=0\\p=0&\text{ or }-\tfrac57\end{aligned}\]\(p\) is a non-zero constant, so \(p=-\frac57\).\[q=-15\times-\frac57=\frac{75}7=10\frac57\]\[p=-\tfrac57,q=10\tfrac57\]

slides.title: Estimating powers

blocks.tex: (a) Find the first four terms of \((1+\frac x4)^8\), in ascending powers of \(x\), giving each term in its simplest form. (4 marks)\par (b) Use the expansion to estimate \(1.025^8\) to four decimal places. (3 marks)
\[\begin{aligned}\left(1+\frac x4\right)^8&=1+\binom81\frac x4+\binom82\left(\frac x4\right)^2+\binom83\left(\frac x4\right)^3+\cdots\\&=1+2x+\frac74x^2+\frac78x^3+\cdots\end{aligned}\]
\[1+\frac x4=1.025\quad\Rightarrow\quad x=0.1\]
Higher powers of \(0.1\) become very small. Compare the estimate with the calculator value.

blocks.tex: (a) Find the first four terms of \((1-3x)^5\), in ascending powers of \(x\), in simplest form. (4 marks)\par (b) For small \(x\), ignore \(x^2\) and higher powers and show that \((1+x)(1-3x)^5\approx1-14x\). (2 marks)

blocks.tex: 9 A microchip company models the probability of having no faulty chips on a single production run as:\[\mathrm P(\text{no fault})=(1-p)^n,\ p<0.001\]where \(p\) is the probability of a single chip being faulty, and \(n\) being the total number of chips produced.\par a State why the model is restricted to small values of \(p\). \hfill\(\text{(1 mar}\ldots\)\par b Given that \(n=200\), find an approximate expression for \(\mathrm P(\text{no fault})\) in the form \(a+bp+cp^2\). \hfill\(\text{(2 mark}\ldots\)\par c The company wants to achieve a \(92\%\) likelihood of having no faulty chips on a production run of 200 chips. Use your answer to part \textbf{b} to suggest a maximum value of \(p\) for this to be the case. \hfill\(\text{(4 mark}\ldots\)

\textbf{a} So that higher powers of p can be ignored as they tend to 0.\par\textbf{b}\[\begin{aligned}(1-p)^{200}&=1^{200}+\binom{200}1 1^{199}(-p)+\binom{200}2 1^{198}(-p)^2+\ldots\\&\approx1-200p+19900p^2\end{aligned}\]\textbf{c}\[\begin{aligned}1-200p+19900p^2&=0.92\\19900p^2-200p+0.08&=0\end{aligned}\]\[p=\frac{-(-200)\pm\sqrt{(-200)^2-4(19900)(0.08)}}{2(19900)}=\frac{200\pm\sqrt{33632}}{39800}\]\(p=0.00963\) or \(p=0.000417\) (to 3 s.f.).\par As \(p<0.001\), the maximum value for \(p\) would be \(0.000417\).
